subtype: Approach: rehearse an earthquake drill at home [Thinking]
passage:
Deepak: So you turned the living room into a drill ground?

Sumit: Kind of! My thinking was simple. In a real shake I won't have time to think, so my body has to already know. I chose the dining table because the legs are thick and it's away from the glass cabinet. Then I checked the two ways out, the front door and the service stairs, and made sure nothing was stacked in front of them. Drop, cover, hold on: down on my knees, under the table, one hand on a leg. My younger brother and sister thought it was a game, so I let them time each other. We did it three Sundays in a row. The third time neither of them asked why any more, they just dropped.

qa.q: Which piece of furniture did Sumit choose for cover?
What did Sumit believe about how the body reacts in a real earthquake?
qa.a: Sumit believed there would be no time to think, so the body has to already know what to do, which shows a wish to feel ready rather than helpless.

qa.q: What could Sumit add to make the drill stronger, and why?
qa.a: Sumit could practise at a different time or in the dark, because a real shake will not wait for a convenient moment.

qa.q: How might Sumit's younger brother see the drill?
qa.a: Sumit's younger brother probably saw it as a game at first, then felt safer as it became automatic.

grounding: Illustrates practising drop, cover and hold on at home, choosing a sturdy table and exits and teaching younger siblings, so panic becomes a learned response.

subtype: Approach: rehearse an earthquake drill at home [Thinking]
passage:
I'm Binita, from the flat next door in Guwahati. Last Sunday I heard a lot of thumping and giggling through the wall, so I went over.
Chandrika had her two little brothers crouched under the heavy dining table. "Drop," she said, and they dropped. "Cover," and they tucked in, arms over their heads. "Hold on," and they grabbed the table legs.
She explained to them out loud, and I think partly to herself: "When the shaking starts, your legs want to run. But running is when things fall on you. So we practise until your body goes to the table without thinking."
Then she walked them to the door and the stairwell, pointing. "Not the lift. Never the lift."
They did it five times. By the fifth, the younger one was under the table before she'd finished saying "drop". I can't know what she was feeling, but she looked serious and satisfied.

qa.q: Which piece of furniture did Chandrika choose for the drill?
qa.a: She chose the heavy dining table.

qa.q: What might Chandrika have been feeling during the drill?
qa.a: She seemed serious and satisfied, perhaps a little worried about a real quake but pleased that her brothers learned quickly.

qa.q: What else could Chandrika add to the family's preparation?
qa.a: She could practise the drill at night too, or in a different room, so the brothers know what to do wherever they are.

qa.q: How might Binita see the drill after watching?
qa.a: Binita, who came because of the noise, may think about practising the same thing in her own flat.

grounding: Shows a student practising drop, cover and hold on, choosing a sturdy table and exits, and teaching younger siblings until it becomes automatic.

subtype: Approach: rehearse an earthquake drill at home [Thinking]
passage:
Saturday. After the small tremor on Thursday, Shalini noticed what she and her little brother Asif had done: they had both run into the corridor. She sat down with a notebook. "Running felt right, but the corridor has the glass cabinet. What should we have done?"
She looked it up in the district disaster guide: get down low, get under something sturdy, and grip it until the shaking stops. Then she walked through the flat, looking for sturdy cover. The study desk, yes. The glass cabinet side, never. The exit: the stairs, not the lift.
Sunday. She practised with Asif. "Drop." He flopped on the floor. "Cover." He crawled under the desk. "Hold on." He grabbed the leg. They did it in his room, the kitchen and the living room.
The next Wednesday. Asif's school ran a surprise drill. That evening he announced, "I was first under the table. My teacher said well done." Shalini just smiled.

qa.q: Where did Shalini look up what to do?
How did Shalini feel after noticing they had both run into the corridor?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and concerned, realising that running took them past the glass cabinet.

qa.q: What else could Shalini do to keep the drill fresh?
qa.a: She could repeat it every few months and include their parents, so the whole family's response stays automatic.

qa.q: How does Asif seem to feel after the school drill?
qa.a: Asif is proud and excited, announcing he was first under the table and the teacher praised him.

grounding: Shows the student rehearsing drop, cover and hold on at home, finding sturdy cover and exits, and teaching a younger sibling.
